messages:
mike: Heads up — seeing a pretty nasty cascade of GPU pod evictions during scheduled node drains in us-west1.
mike: Symptoms: gang-scheduled jobs (4x gpus) fail to reschedule, leftover pods stuck Pending, and then we hit preemption waves across compact pools.
ana: ugh. any obvious scheduler logs or FailedScheduling reason?
mike: See snippet from one of the pods:
```\nEvents:\n  Type     Reason            Age   From               Message\n  ----     ------            ----  ----               -------\n  Normal   Scheduled         2m    default-scheduler  Successfully assigned infra/job-xyz to node-gpu-a\n  Warning  FailedScheduling  30s   default-scheduler  0/12 nodes are available: 6 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate, 4 node(s) didn't match nodeSelector, 2 node(s) had insufficient resources.\n```\n
mike: Also PV claim stuck because local-ssd PVs are node-affine, so the gang can't be placed unless all members land on compatible nodes.
kevin: Are these pods using podAntiAffinity to avoid colocating jobs? could be fighting with gang scheduling.
sophie: Yep, some of these teams set "requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution" anti-affinity to avoid noisy-neighbor colocations. Combined with nodeSelector (nvidia-a100) it's a narrow intersection.
julia: Any recent change to compact pools or taints? I saw a deploy that switched spot handling + a new preemptible-taint last night.
infra-bot: @channel Autoscaler action: scaled down nodepool-gpu-compact-usw1 by 3 nodes at 02:14 UTC due to low avg utilization. (link: https://console.redwood/ops/autoscaler/12345)
mike: That's the kicker — autoscaler removed capacity before the drain plan adjusted for gang sizes. Drains then attempted to reschedule into smaller pool and failed -> eviction cascade.
ana: Can we relax anti-affinity or add fallback soft rules for critical infra jobs? Or introduce a relaxed placement for evicted pods temporarily?
kevin: We could add a scheduling policy: when gang cannot be scheduled for X seconds, allow weight-based soft affinity or bypass nodeSelector to a compatible quantized model variant (a100 -> a10x?)
sophie: For PVs we could switch to use CSI ephemeral volumes for that job class or implement a PV-migration helper — but that's longer term.
julia: Immediate mitigation: hold autoscaler scale-down for gpu-compact-usw1 for 2 hours and start a controlled cordon+drain test on a single node to reproduce without cascading.
infra-bot: @ops Hold request submitted: suspend-scale-down nodepool-gpu-compact-usw1 (ttl: 2h) by julia.
Action ID: HLD-9987
mike: I'll run a quick job to try a canary relocate with relaxed anti-affinity (change to "preferredDuringScheduling") and report back in 15m.
kevin: If that works, we should add an allocator check: refuse autoscaler downscale if there are active gangs that cannot be split and local PV usage > 0.25 on pool.
sophie: Agreed. Also log an alert for "gang-scheduling failure due to taints/selector intersection" so oncall can catch earlier.
ana: I'll open a short RFC for a two-tier mitigation: 1) autoscaler guard, 2) scheduling policy fallback, 3) PV migration plan. Assigning action items.
mike: Quick notes for the RFC: include unit economics impact (we lost ~3 hours of cluster throughput -> estimate $2.1k of queued cycles across customers), list affected jobs (ml-train-prod-*, hypersearch-*) and reproduction steps.
julia: I'll own the autoscaler guard change. kevin can prototype the scheduler fallback. sophie + ana collate PV options.
kevin: ack. will prototype fallback in a feature branch this afternoon.
mike: Thanks all. ping me if you see more evictions. I'll paste results from the canary in this thread.
k8s-drain-bot: Notice: cordon/drain completed on node node-gpu-a-17, 2 pods evicted, 0 pods failed to reschedule.
mike: Canary worked when we switched to preferred anti-affinity — pods rescheduled within 90s into mixed-instance nodes. No PV move needed for the canary (ephemeral test job).
mike: Marking immediate mitigation: suspended autoscaler + recommended scheduling change for affected job classes. Moving RFC to "in-review".
